title: How a planning task flows

nodes.label: API client
nodes.note: Swagger UI, the Postman collection or a script calling the REST API.

nodes.label: Locust and k6 tests
nodes.note: backend/stress-testing: Locust user journeys, a staged k6 script and monitor scripts that hammer the same endpoints.

nodes.label: Timing middleware
nodes.note: core/middleware.py: RequestTimingMiddleware logs method, path, status and latency in ms for every request.

nodes.label: REST routers
nodes.note: api/v1/endpoints: walls, obstacles, tasks, trajectories. POST /tasks returns 202 and hands the work to RabbitMQ.

nodes.label: Cache helpers
nodes.note: core/cache.py: cache_get, cache_set and cache_delete over JSON. Read-through on tasks, walls and trajectories, invalidated on writes.

nodes.label: Queue producer
nodes.note: services/queue_producer.py: pika publisher that declares a durable queue and sends persistent messages.

nodes.label: path_planning_queue
nodes.note: Durable RabbitMQ queue carrying task_id, wall_id and robot_id. Failed messages are rejected without requeue.

nodes.label: Cloud worker
nodes.note: services/cloud_worker.py: consumes one message at a time, sets PROCESSING, runs the planner, saves trajectories, sets COMPLETED or FAILED.

nodes.label: Coverage planner
nodes.note: planning/coverage_planner.py: free space via Shapely, 2m blocks, zigzag sweeps, genetic-algorithm block order, simple detour between blocks.

nodes.label: robot_123_queue
nodes.note: Per-robot command queue. The worker publishes the Standard Sweep waypoints here.

nodes.label: Robot simulator
nodes.note: services/robot_client.py: consumes waypoints, sleeps 2s per move to simulate travel and reports progress after each waypoint.

nodes.label: robot_live_telemetry
nodes.note: Queue the simulator publishes position and progress to. Nothing in this repo consumes it, so it acts as a hook for a future dashboard.

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.note: Caches task_{id} and traj_{id} JSON with a one hour TTL so status polling skips PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL (Neon)
nodes.note: SQLAlchemy models Wall, Obstacle (JSONB geometry), Task and Trajectory (JSONB waypoints). Alembic migrations.

nodes.label: Logstash
nodes.note: Listens on TCP 5959 for JSON logs from python-logstash-async and writes them on to Elasticsearch.

nodes.label: Elasticsearch
nodes.note: Stores one python-logs index per day, including latency, algorithm timing and per-scenario coverage fields.

nodes.label: Kibana
nodes.note: Dashboards over the log index, for request latency and scenario metrics.

flow: A client POSTs a task for a wall. The timing middleware starts a timer and the router checks the wall exists in PostgreSQL.
The router saves the task as PENDING, caches its state in Redis and publishes a persistent message to path_planning_queue, then returns 202 Accepted.
The cloud worker takes one message, marks the task PROCESSING in PostgreSQL and Redis, and loads the wall and its obstacles.
The coverage planner runs three scenarios (tool radius 0.2, 0.5 and 1.0) and the worker saves each trajectory.
The worker marks the task COMPLETED, refreshes the Redis entry and publishes the Standard Sweep waypoints to the robot's queue.
The client polls GET /tasks/{id}, served from Redis, then reads the trajectories from GET /trajectories/{task_id}.
Secondary path: the robot simulator walks the waypoints, publishes progress telemetry, and the API, worker and robot all log JSON through Logstash into Elasticsearch for Kibana.
